Compute document-topic mixtures from segments

Source: R/inference.R
topic_gamma.Rd

topic_gamma() returns, for each document, its mixture over topics: the share of its segments assigned to each topic, the document-topic distribution conventionally called gamma. A document that discusses two subjects in different sentences belongs partly to two topics, which a single embedding of the whole document cannot express; counting the topics of its segments gives the mixture without any additional parameter.

For a model fitted on segments (segment = in topics()) and text = NULL, it counts the fitted assignments, with no encoding. Otherwise it segments the given documents (with the fitted segmentation, or at level), or takes a segment() data frame as it is, embeds the segments, and assigns each to the topic whose unit-length center has the highest cosine similarity, as predict() does. The result is a data frame with one row per document-topic pair.

The fitted assignments come from Lloyd's k-means in topics(), which uses squared Euclidean distance to the raw means of the normalized embeddings; for a few segments on topic boundaries this can differ from the cosine-similarity rule applied to new text. For graded membership of single units, use topic_membership().

Usage

topic_gamma(
  object,
  text = NULL,
  model = NULL,
  embeddings = NULL,
  level = NULL,
  batch_size = 32L,
  cores = 1L,
  dedupe_segments = FALSE,
  sort_by_length = FALSE,
  top = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A fitted model from topics().

text

NULL (default) for the fitted segments of a segmented model; a character vector of documents to segment; or a data frame from segment() (columns document_id and text), used as it is.

model

A model from load_model(), a pinned model name, or NULL (default) for the default model, used to embed the segments; ignored when embeddings are given.

embeddings

Numeric matrix of segment embeddings, one row per segment of text (in the order of segment()), or NULL (default) to encode them.

level

"clause", "sentence", or "phrase" for segmenting a character text, or NULL (default) for the fitted segmentation of a segmented model and "clause" otherwise.

batch_size

Texts per model call when encoding (default 32).

cores

Number of forked processes for segmenting (default 1), passed to segment(); the result does not depend on it.

dedupe_segments

Encode each distinct segment once (default FALSE). Saves time on corpora with many repeated segments; the values can differ from encoding every occurrence by floating-point rounding.

sort_by_length

Batch segments of similar length together when encoding (default FALSE); see encode().

top

NULL (default) for every topic of every document, or a whole number: each document's top largest non-zero shares.

Value

A base data frame with one row per document-topic pair and columns document_id, topic, gamma (the share of the document's segments in the topic), and n_segments. gamma sums to one within each document; documents without segments have no rows. With top, only the largest non-zero shares, ordered by document and share, with a rank column after document_id.

Conditions

sbert_bad_input when text is NULL for a model fitted on whole documents, when model, embeddings or level is given without text, when a data frame lacks document_id or text, when no segment results, or when embeddings has the wrong number of rows; sbert_dimension_mismatch when the embeddings have a different number of columns from the fitted model; when encoding, the conditions of encode().

See also

segment() for the segments; topic_membership() for graded membership; predict() for single assignments; topic_sizes() for topic totals.

Examples

text <- c(
  "Cats chase mice", "Dogs chase balls",
  "Stocks and bonds trade", "Markets price shares"
)
embeddings <- rbind(c(1, 0), c(0.9, 0.1), c(0, 1), c(0.1, 0.9))
fitted <- topics(text, 2, embeddings = embeddings)

# A new document with one sentence on each topic.
mixed <- "Cats chase mice. Stocks and bonds trade."
segment_embeddings <- rbind(c(1, 0), c(0, 1))
topic_gamma(fitted, mixed, embeddings = segment_embeddings)
#>   document_id topic gamma n_segments
#> 1           1     1   0.5          2
#> 2           1     2   0.5          2

# Segment once, then reuse the segments and their embeddings.
segments <- segment(mixed, level = "sentence")
topic_gamma(fitted, segments, embeddings = segment_embeddings)
#>   document_id topic gamma n_segments
#> 1           1     1   0.5          2
#> 2           1     2   0.5          2

# A model fitted on sentences already holds its segments: no text needed.
sentence_model <- topics(
  c(mixed, "Dogs chase balls. Markets price shares."), 2,
  segment = "sentence",
  embeddings = rbind(c(1, 0), c(0, 1), c(0.9, 0.1), c(0.1, 0.9))
)
topic_gamma(sentence_model)
#>   document_id topic gamma n_segments
#> 1           1     1   0.5          2
#> 2           1     2   0.5          2
#> 3           2     1   0.5          2
#> 4           2     2   0.5          2
topic_gamma(sentence_model, top = 1)
#>   document_id rank topic gamma n_segments
#> 1           1    1     1   0.5          2
#> 2           2    1     1   0.5          2
